The business question is how much PAID order revenue is trusted after each daily batch. One output row represents one current order, not one arrival. Write that sentence before writing code. Revenue is qty multiplied by the product unit_price; the order files do not contain a ready-made revenue column. PENDING and CANCELLED orders remain in Silver but contribute zero to paid revenue.
Artifact and completion check
Create docs/source-contract.md. Name the input files, the order_id key, the updated_at version, and the status rule. A reader should be able to calculate one order by hand from your contract.

Why this phase exists
This phase converts one part of the project from an idea into reviewable engineering evidence. Operations needs daily
shipped-order counts, paid revenue and hub-level exception visibility by 07:00. The phase is not complete because a
script ran once; it is complete when another engineer can see the intended grain/state boundary, reproduce the result
and understand how failure is handled.
Before you build
Open the project README and `expected_controls.json`. Work only in your project copy. Preserve supplied raw/failure
fixtures unchanged. Write one sentence naming the invariant for this phase - for example 'accepted + quarantined =
processed input' or 'replay does not change trusted business state' - before changing code.
Teacher checkpoint  -  follow this sequence
1. Read the supplied project brief once without coding.
2. Write the business questions, decision deadline, data consumers and non-functional constraints.
3. List what is evidence versus assumption.
4. Define the exact artifact that will prove the phase complete before creating code.
What must exist when you stop
• Save the genuine first attempt before opening any protected review.
• Keep commands, outputs and at least one validation artifact in the project evidence folder.
• Define the deliverable, expected control and completion evidence before implementation.
• A changed-input retry must still satisfy the invariant.
